summary: Assess coverage gaps and improve delivery for rural and informal workers. Review the five-day course outline and explore enrolment options.
lede: Social protection for rural and informal workers involves identifying coverage gaps and improving access for people with seasonal, mobile or irregular livelihoods. For programme officers, analysts and delivery managers, this means using coverage evidence, comparing contribution options, and reviewing enrolment, payment and grievance pathways. The course applies CODI, ASPIRE and relevant ISPA tools to develop indicators and prioritize practical improvements, including in response to climate-related shocks.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for extending social protection to rural households and workers outside standard payroll systems. It suits intermediate practitioners who contribute to programme analysis, design, delivery or oversight.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with social protection, rural development or informal livelihoods is recommended. No programming is required; basic spreadsheet use will support the indicator exercises.
